recent_posts.title: When AI Tools Get Standing Access: Lessons from the Vercel Breach
recent_posts.summary: The Vercel breach in February 2026 exposed a systemic problem: AI tools with persistent OAuth access become high-value attack vectors. The core issue is standing access — OAuth grants that are always live, credentials always reachable. The recommended fix is Just-in-Time (JIT) access, where OAuth grants only exist during active approved sessions and expire automatically. For AI tooling specifically, JIT can be enforced at the tool invocation level via MCP-connected agents, scoping and time-limiting each action individually. Non-human identities (NHIs) like AI tools and MCP servers are rarely governed with the same rigor as human accounts, creating a growing security gap. A credential injection model — where secrets are injected at connection time and never persist — is proposed as a stronger alternative to secrets classification.

recent_posts.title: Why AI agents need their own identity systems separate from human IAM
recent_posts.summary: Traditional enterprise identity systems were designed around human users—SSO, MFA, and lifecycle management—but AI agents operating autonomously in production environments break these assumptions. Agents use shared service accounts, hardcoded API keys, and credential forwarding, making delegation invisible and accountability ambiguous at scale. StrongDM ID is a new identity provider built specifically for AI agents, allowing developers to register agents with unique verifiable identities and link each to a human sponsor. Built on open identity standards with proof-of-possession mechanisms and token exchange models, it maintains a transparent chain of delegation from human to agent to action, addressing the governance gap that autonomous systems create.

recent_posts.title: The StrongDM Software Factory: Building Software with AI
recent_posts.summary: StrongDM introduces their Software Factory, an AI-driven development approach where humans define intent and scenarios while AI agents generate, validate, and iterate on code autonomously. The system uses scenario-based validation and a Digital Twin Universe to test against real-world behavior, eliminating traditional code review. The factory is now open source and available for developers to experiment with.

recent_posts.title: Universal privileged access authorization closes the authorization gap
recent_posts.summary: Traditional privileged access management based on credential verification is obsolete in modern machine-driven environments. The authorization gap allows compromised credentials to grant extended undetected access. Universal Privileged Access Authorization (UPAA) introduces a new architectural approach with runtime authorization for every action, eliminating standing privileges through continuous policy evaluation across all identities (human, machine, and agent). This control plane unifies access management across hybrid environments, replaces static secrets with dynamic entitlements, and enforces zero standing privilege without disrupting operations.

recent_posts.title: From Authentication to Authorization: The KPI Set Every Board Needs
recent_posts.summary: Real-time authorization has become the critical security control plane as organizations shift from perimeter-based to identity-based security. The article outlines a KPI framework for measuring identity-first security maturity, including metrics for reducing standing credentials, quantifying coverage of critical assets, auditing access drift, and extending oversight to machine and AI agent identities. These measurements help security leaders demonstrate tangible risk reduction and compliance improvements to boards through business-aligned metrics like fewer credential-led incidents, faster containment, and cleaner audits.

recent_posts.title: StrongDM Delivers Policy Enforcement for Agentic AI with Leash
recent_posts.summary: StrongDM released Leash, an open-source project that provides real-time policy enforcement for AI agents. Operating at the kernel level, Leash intercepts agent activity and evaluates it against Cedar-defined policies, offering visibility and control over autonomous workloads. The system monitors agent actions like file access and network calls, enforces context-aware rules before connections are established, and logs all activity for audit purposes. Leash extends StrongDM's access control model from human operators to machine identities, addressing the growing need to govern AI agents that execute unpredictable actions across enterprise networks.

recent_posts.title: StrongDM Debuts in Gartner’s Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management
recent_posts.summary: StrongDM has been recognized in Gartner's Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management, marking a shift from traditional credential vaulting to real-time, policy-based authorization. The platform provides universal access control across databases, servers, clusters, and APIs through continuous authorization rather than static secrets management. StrongDM's architecture enables dynamic policy enforcement, temporary least-privilege access, and granular activity auditing for modern cloud-native and DevOps environments. The recognition validates the evolution of PAM from managing passwords to governing actions across both human and machine identities in distributed, ephemeral infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: AI Agents Are Actors, Not Tools: Why Enterprises Need a New Layer of Runtime Governance
recent_posts.summary: AI agents operate autonomously with system-level privileges, creating security risks that traditional governance models can't address. Enterprises need runtime governance that monitors agent behavior at the kernel level using technologies like eBPF, enforces context-aware policies through languages like AWS Cedar, and provides immediate containment capabilities. This approach enables real-time observation and enforcement of agent actions—from file access to network calls—ensuring safe autonomy from development through production deployment.

recent_posts.title: Managing Access Drift: Introducing Entitlement Visibility, Resource Discovery, and JIT for Microsoft Cloud
recent_posts.summary: StrongDM announces three new features to address cloud access management challenges: Entitlement Visibility for real-time tracking of all permissions including temporary and JIT access, Resource Discovery for automatic scanning and onboarding of AWS, GCP, and Azure resources, and Just-in-Time Access for Microsoft Cloud to eliminate standing privileges in Azure, Entra ID, and Microsoft 365. These capabilities aim to replace manual access management processes with an automated, identity-aware control plane that provides unified visibility and Zero Trust access across dynamic cloud environments.

recent_posts.title: Essential devsecops tools for securing modern development workflows
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to eight essential DevSecOps tools covering infrastructure access control, code security, CI/CD pipeline protection, container runtime security, secrets management, code-to-cloud security, fine-grained authorization, and threat detection. The guide explains how each tool secures different layers of the development stack and emphasizes the importance of unified access control through Zero Trust and least privilege principles. It includes practical use cases, integration patterns, and a case study demonstrating how these tools work together to enable security-first teams to build and deploy applications quickly while maintaining compliance and visibility.
